note: Curated source catalog. Every feed here was fetched and parsed with this plugin's own parser before being listed. Organized into bundles so setup can offer taste rather than a blank text box.
principle: This surface gets a few seconds of involuntary attention, so anything you'd encounter through your normal channels anyway is wasted width. Nothing here is a general tech-news site: you will see those stories regardless. Preference goes to independent and worker-owned outlets, writers with a distinctive angle, and archives deep enough to sample rather than feeds that only tell you what happened in the last hour.

modes.recent: Take the newest items, filtered by age. Right for outlets that are genuinely publishing news.
modes.evergreen: Sample anywhere in the feed's archive, ignoring age. Right for writers whose five-year-old post is as good as today's — which is most of the best ones.

indie.label: Independent & worker-owned
indie.why: Outlets that answer to their writers rather than to a traffic target. Low volume, high hit rate, and they break stories the trade press won't touch.

feeds.label: 404 Media
feeds.why: Worker-owned tech reporting; the surveillance and platform-abuse stories nobody else runs.

feeds.label: Defector
feeds.why: Ex-Deadspin staff, employee-owned. Sports as a way into everything else.

feeds.label: Aftermath
feeds.why: Worker-owned games criticism, written by people with no publisher to please.

feeds.label: Rest of World
feeds.why: Technology outside the US and Europe — consistently the least duplicated reporting in this list.

feeds.label: Molly White
feeds.why: Rigorous, receipts-first accountability writing on crypto and tech power.

feeds.label: Anil Dash
feeds.why: Twenty-five years of writing about what the web is for.

deep-eng.label: Deep engineering
deep-eng.why: People who explain a system all the way down rather than summarizing a press release. Most of these have archives worth sampling at random.

feeds.label: Julia Evans
feeds.why: Makes hard systems topics genuinely legible without dumbing them down.

feeds.label: Dan Luu
feeds.why: Empirical and contrarian; checks the claims everyone else repeats. 128-post archive.

feeds.label: Bartosz Ciechanowski
feeds.why: The best explanatory writing on the internet. Posts rarely; every one is worth the wait.

feeds.label: Ken Shirriff
feeds.why: Reverse-engineers silicon under a microscope — Apollo hardware, 1970s chips.

feeds.label: Fabien Sanglard
feeds.why: Game engine and hardware teardowns. 144-post archive.

feeds.label: Hillel Wayne
feeds.why: Formal methods and what software engineering research actually shows.

feeds.label: Simon Willison
feeds.why: The most reliable running commentary on what LLMs can currently do.

feeds.label: Cloudflare
feeds.why: Real postmortems and protocol work at a scale most of us never see.

feeds.label: Nicole Tietz
feeds.why: Software craft and the human side of it. 218-post archive.

feeds.label: Erik Bernhardsson
feeds.why: Data infrastructure with unusually good instincts about what matters. 172 posts.

feeds.label: Brandur
feeds.why: Careful long-form on Postgres, APIs, and idempotency.

feeds.label: Xe Iaso
feeds.why: Infrastructure writing with a voice.

feeds.label: Lobsters
feeds.why: Hacker News without the startup noise; a much higher technical floor.

science.label: Science, properly done
science.why: Including two feeds about how science goes wrong, which is usually more instructive than the press releases.

feeds.label: Quanta
feeds.why: Maths and physics reporting that respects the actual result.

feeds.label: In the Pipeline
feeds.why: Derek Lowe on drug discovery, including the legendary 'Things I Won't Work With'. 100-post archive.

feeds.label: Retraction Watch
feeds.why: Where the scientific record gets corrected. A running education in how fraud works.

feeds.label: Andrew Gelman
feeds.why: Statistics done in public, mistakes included. 50-post archive.

feeds.label: Nautilus
feeds.why: Long-form science essays with room to breathe.

feeds.label: Undark
feeds.why: Science journalism that reports on the institutions, not just the findings.

feeds.label: APOD
feeds.why: One astronomy picture a day, explained by astronomers. Running since 1995.

history-culture.label: History & culture
history-culture.why: The strongest argument for evergreen sampling — a good post about the twelfth century does not get less relevant.

feeds.label: ACOUP
feeds.why: Bret Devereaux on pre-modern logistics and warfare. Unreasonably good on how societies actually fed armies.

feeds.label: Public Domain Review
feeds.why: Beautiful, strange artefacts out of copyright. 100-item archive.

feeds.label: JSTOR Daily
feeds.why: Scholarship translated for people who won't read the paper, with the paper linked.

feeds.label: Language Log
feeds.why: Linguists puncturing linguistic myths, often the ones you believe.

ideas.label: Ideas & essays
ideas.why: Longer arguments worth carrying around. Deliberately spans positions rather than one house style.

feeds.label: Aeon
feeds.why: Philosophy and science essays, edited hard.

feeds.label: Psyche
feeds.why: Aeon's psychology sibling; practical without being self-help.

feeds.label: Asterisk
feeds.why: Numerate essays on questions most magazines handle badly.

feeds.label: Noema
feeds.why: Technology and governance at civilizational scale.

feeds.label: Crooked Timber
feeds.why: Academics arguing in public, well.

feeds.label: Marginal Revolution
feeds.why: High-volume economics links; unusually good at surfacing the obscure.

feeds.label: Astral Codex Ten
feeds.why: Long, argumentative, frequently wrong in interesting ways.

feeds.label: The Marginalian
feeds.why: Literature and science read together, with real archive depth.

feeds.label: Reasons to be Cheerful
feeds.why: Solutions journalism — what's actually working somewhere. A useful corrective.

feeds.label: Longreads
feeds.why: Curation rather than a publication; the best of everyone else's archive.

how-things-work.label: How things get built
how-things-work.why: Physical-world engineering. A reliable antidote to a day spent entirely inside software.

feeds.label: Construction Physics
feeds.why: Brian Potter on why building anything got so expensive.

feeds.label: Practical Engineering
feeds.why: Civil infrastructure explained by someone who builds it.

feeds.label: The Pudding
feeds.why: Visual essays that could not exist in any other medium.

curious.label: Genuinely odd
curious.why: The bundle most likely to produce something you'd never have gone looking for, which is the whole point of the surface.

feeds.label: Damn Interesting
feeds.why: Meticulously researched forgotten episodes of history.

feeds.label: Low-tech Magazine
feeds.why: Pre-industrial technology taken seriously. The site runs on a solar-powered server and goes offline when it's cloudy.

feeds.label: Atlas Obscura
feeds.why: Places and practices that shouldn't exist but do.

feeds.label: Futility Closet
feeds.why: Puzzles, curiosities, and lateral historical oddities.

feeds.label: Kottke
feeds.why: Twenty-five years of one person with excellent taste linking things.

feeds.label: MetaFilter
feeds.why: The last good community weblog; posts are researched before they're posted.

feeds.label: Web Curios
feeds.why: A weekly tour of the internet's far corners, written with genuine style.

feeds.label: Nicky Case
feeds.why: Explorable explanations about systems, cooperation, and minds.

feeds.label: Sentiers
feeds.why: Futures and complexity, curated by someone reading more widely than you are.
